# Own-depth potentials: inner-level geometry, exact laws, and a selection obstruction

The joint concavity of the own-fiber depth root is already in
candidate 325d279c18e3a49e and is implicit in
continuous-depth-brunn-minkowski.md. It is not a new OC mechanism
by itself; the former note exactly disproves the associated capacity
principle on actual compatible triangle fibers.

The additional conclusions here are an equality criterion, explicit
simplex level geometry, an exact planar level-volume law, and an
actual-source obstruction to fixed high-depth-level selection.
Absolute levels and relative levels behave differently.

## 1. Joint concavity, closed absolute levels, and equality

Let C be compact and convex in R^n x R^d, d>=1. For each real base z
and x in its nonempty fiber K_z define

    f(z,x)=inf_(|u|=1) |K_z intersect {y:u.y>=u.x}|,
    F(z,x)=f(z,x)^(1/d).

These use full d-dimensional fiber volume. A lower-dimensional fiber
has F identically zero. Then F is nonnegative, upper semicontinuous,
and jointly concave on C.

Indeed, like-oriented through-point caps satisfy

    (1-t)[K_z0 intersect {u.y>=u.x0}]
      +t[K_z1 intersect {u.y>=u.x1}]
      subset K_zt intersect {u.y>=u.xt},

where (zt,xt) is the convex combination of the two source points.
All sets are nonempty, since their respective center points belong
to them. Brunn--Minkowski applies even when an endpoint volume is
zero. Taking roots and then the infimum over u proves concavity.

For upper semicontinuity, fix u and let (z_k,x_k)->(z,x) in C.
Every subsequential limit of the corresponding compact cap sets
belongs to the limiting cap set, because C and the inequalities
are closed. The sets are uniformly bounded, so eventually they
lie in every fixed outer parallel neighborhood of that limiting
set. Continuity from above of the neighborhood volumes bounds
their limsup volume by the limiting volume. Taking the infimum
over u proves upper semicontinuity of F, including boundary bases.

Consequently

    D_r={(z,x) in C:F(z,x)>=r},  r>=0,

and the hypograph {(z,x,r):0<=r<=F(z,x)} are compact convex sets.
For fixed r, the dth root of the volumes |(D_r)_z| is concave on
the projection of D_r, with nonempty endpoint sections. It is not
asserted to remain concave after extension by zero outside that
projection. A nonempty integer section can have zero d-volume,
for example at a fiber's highest own-depth level.

There is also an exact equality criterion when 0<t<1 and both
endpoint F-values are positive. Equality in joint concavity holds
if and only if there is a common normal u such that:

1. its endpoint caps are active own-depth caps;
2. those two caps are positively homothetic, with volume-root
   ratio F(z1,x1)/F(z0,x0);
3. their weighted Minkowski sum equals the entire target cap.

Necessity follows by choosing an attaining normal at the target
and inspecting the inclusion/BM/depth inequality chain. Every
inequality must be equality. Positive-volume convex inclusion
with equal volume is equality of sets. Conversely these three
conditions give the opposite inequality to joint concavity.
The homothety maps x0 to x1: the exposed bottom faces of the active
caps are their through-point sections, whose centroids equal the
points by the audited active-section-centroid lemma.

This is a criterion for active caps. It does not force the entire
endpoint fibers to be homothetic at arbitrary nonmaximizing points.

## 2. Exact simplex rays and all-dimensional high-level shapes

Let T be a d-simplex, with volume V, centroid g, barycentrics
lambda_i, m=d+1, and Gamma=(d/m)^d. Its maximum own depth is
Gamma V, uniquely attained at g.

On every vertex-to-centroid segment there is the exact formula

    f_T(v_i+t(g-v_i))=Gamma V t^d,  0<=t<=1.          (1)

The homothetic simplex v_i+t(T-v_i) is contained in T and has
the displayed point as centroid, giving the lower bound. The
original vertex-i cap with edge ratio d t/(d+1) passes through
that point and has precisely that volume, giving the upper bound.
Thus the depth root is exactly affine on these segments; joint
concavity is not strict even within a fixed simplex.

The full-depth regions are not generally smaller homothetic copies
of T. For all tau sufficiently close to Gamma from below, they
have the exact description

    {x in T:f_T(x)>=tau V}
      ={lambda_i>=0, sum lambda_i=1:
           d^d product_(j!=i) lambda_j>=tau for every i}.       (2)

The local vertex-cap formula and all-normal localization needed
here are proved in candidate 3795aff5f3322d52,
Sections 2-3, at zero truncation. For completeness, the canonical
upper cap bound forces any depth-tau point to satisfy
max lambda_i<=1-tau^(1/d), hence to approach the centroid as
tau increases to Gamma. Conversely, any point satisfying the
product inequalities also has this bound: for an index of the
largest barycentric coordinate, AM-GM on the other d coordinates
gives d^d product_(j!=i)lambda_j<=(1-lambda_i)^d.
Both sets are therefore in the same neighborhood where the
exact all-normal formula applies.

An explicit sharp high-level asymptotic follows. As e decreases
to zero,

    (Gamma/e)({f_T>=(Gamma-e)V}-g)
                       -> -(T-g) in Hausdorff distance,
    |{f_T>=(Gamma-e)V}|/V
                       =(e/Gamma)^d(1+O_d(e)).      (3)

To check the constant, write lambda_i=1/m+delta_i. The preceding
bound gives delta_i=O_d(e), uniformly on the region. Its i-th
product is Gamma-m Gamma delta_i+O_d(e^2). The region is therefore
sandwiched between the two zero-sum barycentric simplexes
delta_i<=e/(m Gamma) +/- C_d e^2. Their rescalings converge to
the reflected centered simplex, and their volume ratios are
(e/Gamma)^d(1+O_d(e)). This proves (3) with a dimension-only
constant, after affine normalization. It concerns own-depth
levels, not a mixed maximum-depth asymptotic.

## 3. The complete planar level-volume law

For a triangle, order the barycentrics A>=B>=C. The all-direction
ordinary formula, independently proved in
candidate 4ffd81a5b3e6f9fb,
Section 1, is

    f_T(x)=4BC V.

For 0<tau<=4/9 set

    a_tau=(1-sqrt(1-2tau))/2,
    b_tau=sqrt(tau)/2.

Then the exact fraction of triangle area at own depth at least
tau V is

    psi(tau)=1-3a_tau-3tau log(b_tau/a_tau).         (4)

Set psi(0)=1 and psi(4/9)=0. Here is a direct integration.
In one ordered barycentric chamber,

    0<=C<=1/3,  C<=B<=(1-C)/2.

Uniform barycentric probability has density 2, and six chambers
cover the triangle up to null boundaries. The additional condition
4BC>=tau gives

    psi(tau)=12[
       integral_(a_tau)^(b_tau)
           ((1-C)/2-tau/(4C)) dC
       +integral_(b_tau)^(1/3) (1-3C)/2 dC].

Using 2a_tau(1-a_tau)=tau reduces this expression to (4).
The limiting conventions follow directly from the integral.
Every positive nonmaximal level is a strictly convex region with
piecewise hyperbolic boundary; it is not a triangle.

The exact layer-cake first moment is

    integral_T f_T(x) dx=(7/54)V^2.                 (5)

Equivalently integral_0^(4/9) psi(tau)d tau=7/54.
This follows without integrating the logarithm:

    12 integral_0^(1/3) integral_C^((1-C)/2) 4BC dB dC=7/54.

Every triangle inner level has centroid g. All permutations of
the triangle vertices preserve its own-depth function and the
region, and their only common fixed point is g. In particular
fixed relative levels have area psi(tau)V and retain the exact
original centroid at every affine triangle fiber.

## 4. What layer cake recovers, and what it does not

For any full-dimensional convex K, let A=max f_K and W_s={f_K>=s}.
For every measurable H the exact layer-cake identity is

    integral_0^A |W_s intersect H| ds
                         =integral_(K intersect H) f_K(x) dx.  (6)

It recovers the DEPTH-WEIGHTED original measure, not uniform
volume. For triangle fibers (5) implies
sum_z integral_(K_z) f_Kz=(7/54)sum_z |K_z|^2.
This is not a constant times the original total mixed mass.

A general comparison follows from concavity of F=f_K^(1/d).
If g_* is its unique maximum point and 0<=s<=A, then

    g_*+[1-(s/A)^(1/d)](K-g_*) subset W_s,
    |W_s|>=V[1-(s/A)^(1/d)]^d.                      (7)

For a fixed nonzero normal, its upper-cap volume at uniform x
is uniform on [0,V]. Since f_K(x) is bounded by both opposing
cap volumes, also

    |W_s|<=max(V-2s,0).                             (8)

Integrating gives

    VA/binom(2d,d) <= integral_K f_K <= V^2/4.       (9)

The lower constant is exact for the class of nonnegative concave
depth-root-shaped potentials with zero boundary values: take the
linear gauge tent about an interior point, whose every level is
the homothetic set in (7). It is not asserted sharp within actual
own-depth roots in d>=2. Both constants are exact for intervals.
Formula (5) is an exact actual-depth constant for triangles.

Nor can uniform volume be represented by a nontrivial positive
mixture of uniform inner-body laws. Precisely, if a probability
mixture of the normalized volume measures on W_s, for
0<=s<A, equals uniform volume on K, it must put all its mass at
s=0. To see this, its density at x is the nondecreasing function
integral_[0,f_K(x)] |W_s|^(-1) d eta(s). For small r>0,
|W_s| is bounded below uniformly for s<=r. Let f_K(x) decrease
to zero through positive-volume boundary layers. The displayed
density then tends to eta({0})/V. Equality to 1/V almost everywhere
forces eta({0})=1. A possible mass at s=A would be singular at
the unique deepest point and likewise cannot occur.

Thus a positive average of uniform inner bodies cannot silently
replace the original uniform law. Surface disintegrations or
nonconstant weights are different constructions.

## 5. Relative levels need not have a convex graph

Absolute F levels are convex by Section 1. Relative levels
f_Kz(x)>=tau |K_z| need not be.

For an actual interval family at real -1<=z<=1 take

    K_z=[0,2-|z|].

At any fixed 0<tau<1/2 its relative inner interval is
[tau(2-|z|),(1-tau)(2-|z|)]. The two points (-1,tau)
and (1,tau) lie on the relative level, while their midpoint
(0,tau) lies strictly below the middle lower endpoint 2tau.
The graph is therefore nonconvex. Normalization by the own
maximum produces the same example after rescaling tau.

## 6. An exact fixed high-level selection obstruction

Use the actual rational triangle source of
candidate 84ed2ea21a94e03a:

    T=conv(0,e1,e2), V=1/2,
    B=conv((0,0),(4/5,0),(0,8/25)),
    eta=2^-20, s=3/128+eta,
    K_-=(2-s)B, K_0=T, K_+=sB

at bases -1,0,+1. Write a=|K_-|, b=|K_+| and M=a+V+b.
The archive proves exact fibers, nonheavy masses, and q=d=2.
In particular a>V>b and M/2-a=1/4096000.

Fix the rational constants

    delta=2^-30, k=2/3-delta, theta=k/(2/3).

Retain ALL source points satisfying the same relative level

    f_Kz(x)>=k^2 |K_z|.                              (10)

Every one of these three retained sets has positive area: its
centroid has depth (4/9)|K_z| strictly above this level. Yet
EVERY retained integer point has actual mixed depth below
(Gamma_2/2)M.

Indeed each canonical own cap gives
(1-lambda_i(x))^2>=k^2, so all barycentrics are at most
1/3+delta and, by their sum, at least 1/3-2delta.
On K_-, therefore, the fixed cap

    y-2(z+1)>=(2-s)(8/25)(1/3-2delta)

contains the entire retained region and isolates its fiber.
Its actual mass is (2/3+2delta)^2 a. The analogous cap

    y+2(z-1)>=s(8/25)(1/3-2delta)

does the same on K_+, with mass (2/3+2delta)^2 b.
Both are below the target. For the larger a, the original
centroid-cap gap is 1/9216000, while the increase is
[(8/3)delta+4delta^2]a<3delta<1/9216000.

For the middle fiber put e=b/V,

    h=1/3-(17/52)e,  beta=(8/25)(1-s).

The old fixed cap {y+beta z>=h} excludes both endpoint fibers
and has mass V(1-h)^2 below the target. It contains the entire
middle retained region because

    1/3-2delta-h=10268075793/223338299392000>0.

These three explicit closed caps certify the assertion for ALL
points of the retained regions, not just their centroids.

There is also a common ABSOLUTE level counter on the same source.
Retain F>=k sqrt(a), equivalently f>=k^2 a. Exact arithmetic gives
k^2 a>(4/9)V>(4/9)b, so only the left integer fiber survives.
Its retained set is the same positive-area left set just shown
to be entirely bad. This is the fixed fractional near-peak rule
F>=theta max_(integer source)F, with the displayed universal
rational theta<1. Absolute-level convexity is fully consistent
with this failure to contain a target-depth integer point.

More generally, the centroid of any positive-area triangle
inner level is its original centroid. Therefore replacing the
fibers by such levels and selecting only convex combinations
of their centroids stays inside the already refuted centroid
convex-hull selector, regardless of the level weights.

These examples refute the specified high-level restrictions.
They do not refute every lower level, arbitrary transport
constructed from the potential, or OC.

The companion verifier is
verify_own_depth_inner_level_laws_and_selection_obstruction.py.
